topic.title: Translating an Oxygen user manual
topic.shortdesc: Use this procedure to translate a user manual into a new language, or to update an existing translation.

body.p: The translation process includes the next steps: create a translation branch, translate user manual, review and update the translation, integrate the translation branch and optional publish it.

A translation branch lets you work on a translation without changing the source content. When reviewing the translation, you compare the source-language topic with the translated topic. The source-language topic must remain unchanged during this review.
As example I will translate the Content Fusion Cloud manual into French (fr-FR).
Open Content Fusion in your browser, go to User Guide project and in your workspace and create a new branch. You can named it for instance translation/translate--<product>--<lang>.
Do all the work in the next steps on this branch.
You use these values in every step. Write them down before you start.

ul.li:
Product name: the product, exactly as listed in the Products table of .contentfusion/i18n/agent-instructions.md.
Example: Content Fusion Cloud

<product>: the folder that holds the product's language resources.
Example: fusion

<lang>: the target language, as a BCP 47 tag (with a hyphen).
Example: fr-FR

<lang_>: the same language with an underscore. UI strings file names use this form.
Example: fr_FR

Output folder: the folder that receives the translated files.
Example: DITA-cf/i18n/fusion-cloud/fr-FR/

Ticket: the Jira ticket for the work.
Example: CF-1234

body.p: The translation agent reads three files from .contentfusion/i18n/:

ul.li: agent-instructions.md: the rules the agent applies to every translation.

<product>/terminology/terminology.en-US-<lang>.md: approved terms and terms that must not be translated.
Example: fusion/terminology/terminology.en-US-fr-FR.md

<product>/terminology/ui-strings.<lang_>.md: the product's translated UI labels.
Example: fusion/terminology/ui-strings.fr_FR.md

body.note: If the terminology or UI strings file is missing for a language, the agent still translates, but the quality is lower.
body.p: Do these tasks to make sure the files are present and up to date.

ol.li: Get the latest XML UI strings for the product. Follow the instructions on the Oxygen i18n wiki page.

Save the XML files in translation/xml-translation/<product>/.
Example: translation/xml-translation/fusion/

topic.title: 3.2 Convert the UI strings to Markdown

body.p: The agent can't read the XML files. Convert them to Markdown with the translation/ui-strings-to-md.xsl stylesheet.

ul.li: Option A: Run the script. Needs Java 11 or later and Saxon-HE 12.
Option B: Run the stylesheet in Oxygen XML Editor. No extra installs: Oxygen XML Editor includes Saxon.

body.p: Both options write one ui-strings.<lang_>.md file for each language in the XML files.

ol.li:
Open the script in a text editor:
Windows: translation\ui-strings-to-md.bat
Linux, macOS, or Git Bash: translation/ui-strings-to-md.sh

In the Settings section at the top of the script, check these variables. Relative paths start from the translation folder.
IN_DIR: the folder with the XML files from step 3.1.
Example: xml-translation/fusion
OUT_DIR: the product's terminology folder.
Example: ../.contentfusion/i18n/fusion/terminology
SAXON_LIB: leave it empty if Saxon-HE 12 is in your local Maven repository (~/.m2/repository). Otherwise, set it to the folder of the Saxon-HE 12 download (the folder with the Saxon jar and its lib/ subfolder).
To use other folders for one run without editing the script, pass them as arguments: translation\ui-strings-to-md.bat in=<input folder> out=<output folder>

Run the script. You can run it from any folder.
Windows: translation\ui-strings-to-md.bat
Linux, macOS, or Git Bash: translation/ui-strings-to-md.sh
The script lists each file it writes. It also warns about strings that have no translation in a language.
If the script stops with an ERROR: line, fix the cause and run it again. Common causes: Java or Saxon is not found, or the input folder is wrong.
Check the diff of the Markdown files, then commit them.

topic.title: Option B: Run the stylesheet in Oxygen XML Editor

ol.li: In Oxygen XML Editor, open translation/ui-strings-to-md.xsl.

Create a transformation scenario:
Select Configure Transformation Scenario(s), then NewXSLT transformation.
Leave the XML URL field empty.
Set Transformer to Saxon-HE, PE, or EE, version 12 or later.
In the Saxon advanced options, set Initial template to xsl:initial-template.

Click Parameters and set these parameters. Relative paths start from the translation folder.
in: the folder with the XML files from step 3.1.
Example: xml-translation/fusion/
out: the product's terminology folder.
Example: ../.contentfusion/i18n/fusion/terminology/

Apply the scenario.
The Markdown files are written to the out folder. Warnings about missing translations appear in the Results panel.
Check the diff of the Markdown files, then commit them.

body.p: Skip this task if the product is already in the Products table of .contentfusion/i18n/agent-instructions.md.
Otherwise, add a row to that table with the product name and its <product> folder.
body.note: If the product is not in the table, the agent stops before it translates anything.

ol.li: Open the User Guide project in Content Fusion.

Start a translation. In the prompt, name the product and the output folder.
Example: Translations are for product: `Content Fusion Cloud`.
Save translations to `DITA-cf/i18n/fusion-cloud/fr-FR/`, mirroring the source structure inside it.
Open translation/review-prompt.md.

In the Variables section, set TARGET_LANG to the target language.
Example: TARGET_LANG = fr-FR

Give the prompt to the AI assistant.
The reviewer compares each translated file with its source. It writes a report to translation-review-<lang>.md at the repository root.
Read the report. Start with the root-cause rollup: a few root causes usually explain most of the issues.

Fix the issues:
Root causes: fix them in the terminology file or in agent-instructions.md. Then translate the affected files again.
One-off issues: fix them directly in the translated file.
Commit all changes to the translation branch.

body.p: In Content Fusion, integrate the translation branch.
